findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_verifiers, check_audit_exemption · Private data: list_verifiers, check_audit_exemption · Public sink: check_audit_exemption, share_with_openaccountants · Destructive: search_skills, start.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_verifiers, check_audit_exemption · Private data: list_verifiers, check_audit_exemption · Public sink: check_audit_exemption, share_with_openaccountants · Destructive: search_skills, start

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_rules" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

Best for cross-cutting questions — 'VAT rates in MT, IE and DE', 'all income-tax thresholds for 2025', 'rules mentioning reverse charge'. WHEN YOU WANT ONE SPECIFIC FIG"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
